summary.text: Rashida Tlaib is the Democratic incumbent for Michigan's 12th District. A Detroit native and attorney, she served in the Michigan House from 2009 to 2015 and has been in Congress since January 2019. She has campaigned on Medicare for All and a $15 minimum wage.

paragraphs.text: Born and raised in Detroit, the oldest of 14 children of Palestinian immigrant parents, according to her House biography; graduated from Southwestern High School in 1994.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Wayne State University (1998) and a law degree from Western Michigan University Thomas M. Cooley Law School (2004).
Worked as a staffer for former state Rep. Steve Tobocman and as an attorney with nonprofit legal advocacy groups, including the Sugar Law Center for Economic and Social Justice.
Elected to the Michigan House of Representatives in 2008 and served from 2009 to 2015; her House biography says she was the first Muslim woman to serve in the Michigan Legislature.
Ran for Michigan State Senate District 4 in the 2014 Democratic primary and lost to incumbent Virgil Smith, 41.9% to 49.8%.

Won election to the U.S. House in 2018 from Michigan's 13th District, taking office January 3, 2019; she and Ilhan Omar were the first Muslim women to serve in Congress. She has represented the 12th District since 2023.

Serves on the House Financial Services Committee (including its Oversight and Investigations and Housing and Insurance subcommittees) and the House Oversight Committee, and chairs the Congressional Mamas' Caucus and the Get the Lead Out Caucus.

Her House biography credits her with the 'We Have A Right To Breathe' campaign over truck traffic in Detroit neighborhoods and with testing and calling attention to petroleum coke on the Detroit riverfront.
Won the Democratic primary for the 12th District on August 4, 2026, with 69.4% of the vote.
